sources.title: Grok Code Fast 1 announcement, August 28, 2025
sources.evidence: Original announcement identifies exact model, coding-focused pretraining/post-training, reasoning and tools, and a new architecture without defining its topology or count. It confirms the prior public sonic stealth release, during which multiple checkpoints were deployed, and states a multimodal variant was still in training.

sources.title: Grok Code Fast 1 Model Card, August 26, 2025
sources.evidence: Read six-page original card through indexed PDF retrieval; terminal download returned 403. Exact model is a coding reasoning model with iterative tool calls and hosted API/partner distribution. Training and safety evaluations disclose no numerical total or active size and no neural-network topology.

sources.title: Grok Code Out Now, August 26, 2025
sources.evidence: Official Announcements topic by Kody Fisher explicitly identifies grok-code-fast-1 as available and identifies it as the earlier sonic ghost model. This is earlier than the current xAI August 28 announcement dateline.

sources.title: Sonic public preview discussion, August 20, 2025
sources.evidence: Provider admin note confirms public free sonic testing with 256k context. Staff replies on August 20 say it is a partner model, not a Cursor-trained model. The later official Cursor announcement and xAI announcement establish its Grok Code Fast 1 identity. Community speculation about another Cursor MoE kernel project is not model evidence.

sources.title: Lee Robinson announces public stealth model, August 20, 2025
sources.evidence: Original X JSON identifies Lee Robinson and timestamp 2025-08-20T01:26:54.000Z. He announces a new partner stealth model in Cursor, free to try. Canonical post https://x.com/leerob/status/1957977611646439628. Used with the explicitly linked sonic identity, not alone.

sources.title: Grok Code Fast 1 public preview in Copilot, August 26, 2025
sources.evidence: Primary partner changelog confirms named-model public preview beginning August 26. Its September 2 editorial update concerns the end of complimentary access, not initial release.

sources.title: xAI Grok Code Fast 1 historical specifications
sources.evidence: Exact original model documentation specifies 256000 prompt-plus-response tokens, text-only input/output, function calling and reasoning. It explicitly excludes images, audio, video and document files. Provider retirement dates are distinct from xAI API redirects.

sources.title: Grok Code Fast 1 in Microsoft Foundry
sources.evidence: Exact model catalog corroborates text input/output, 256k context and function calling. Description repeats new architecture without specifying topology or parameter count. Provider output limit is not confused with full context.

sources.title: Current native slug resolves to Grok Build 0.1
sources.evidence: Fresh HTML at the original URL now contains model grok-build-0.1, with grok-code-fast-1 and grok-code-fast-1-0825 as aliases, and image input. This is replacement routing, not evidence that original Code Fast 1 weights had image capability.

sources.title: May 15, 2026 retirement and code-model redirect
sources.evidence: Specific code-workload section and table state grok-code-fast-1 is retired and redirected to grok-build-0.1. Generic preceding text mentions grok-4.3 for retired slugs; the model-specific row and current exact alias payload identify Build 0.1. No original specifications are inherited from either replacement.

sources.title: Enterprise terms effective at original launch
sources.evidence: Release-period terms give limited hosted API access and retain rights to underlying technology with xAI or suppliers. Supports proprietary classification; no model-weight redistribution license.

sources.title: Official public checkpoint inventory
sources.evidence: Fresh public organization inventory contains Grok-1 and Grok-2 only, not Grok Code Fast 1. Corroborates original hosted distribution and proprietary terms; absence is not used as the sole evidence.

sources.title: Frontier AI Framework and data disclosure, December 2025
sources.evidence: Primary data-disclosure appendix explicitly names Grok Code Fast 1 and approximately September 2024 training start. It discusses training data and methods, not size or network architecture; training-start date is not public availability.

sources.evidence: Checked complete cached original PDF text, training sections and comparison material for exact Code Fast 1 references and parameter/architecture disclosures. No exact-model count or topology is supplied; later Grok sibling specifications are not transferred.

sources.evidence: Checked complete cached original PDF text, training sections and comparison material for exact Code Fast 1 references and parameter/architecture disclosures. No exact-model count or topology is supplied; later Grok sibling specifications are not transferred.

sources.title: Grok 4.7 model card, September 21
sources.evidence: Checked complete cached original PDF text, training sections and comparison material for exact Code Fast 1 references and parameter/architecture disclosures. No exact-model count or topology is supplied; later Grok sibling specifications are not transferred.

sources.title: Third-party 314B and MoE claims
sources.evidence: Indexed page asserts 314B and MoE plus detailed layer dimensions, but its cited original announcement and card do not establish those claims for this model. Other directories even label the same figure dense. Recorded as an unsupported secondary conflict, not technical evidence.

name.note: Normalize the imported provider-like label to the exact developer model name.

developer.note: Original developer named on the release and model card; Cursor was a distribution partner for this model.

family.note: Grok coding family; do not infer shared weights or topology from another Grok release.

release_date.note: Earliest documented public preview as sonic, later explicitly identified as Grok Code Fast 1 by both xAI and Cursor. Named Cursor/Copilot release was August 26; current xAI announcement is dated August 28. Preview checkpoints changed, so this does not assert identical preview and final weights. September 2 baseline is not the debut.

open_weights.note: Original distribution was hosted API and partner access; no public exact-model checkpoint found. Public safety prompts are not model weights.

license.note: Descriptive classification of model access under release-period proprietary service terms, not an SPDX weights license.

parameters_b.note: No supported total count in accessed primary release, original/later cards or training disclosures. Targeted founder/researcher searches found no exact-model numerical disclosure. The secondary 314B claim is not substantiated by the cited original material and is not imported from Grok-1.

active_parameters_b.note: No exact-model active-per-token count found in primary material or targeted disclosure searches. Speed, compact-model language and serving optimizations do not establish a count.

architecture.note: Original developer says a new architecture built from scratch without naming dense, MoE, Transformer or a layer layout. Targeted training/interpretability research and later cards supplied no exact-model topology. Secondary 314B/MoE claims and unrelated Cursor MoE kernel research are not adopted.

context_window.note: Original Code Fast 1 context is 256000 prompt-plus-response tokens, independently documented by historical providers and the preview admin note. Not inferred from replacement Build 0.1.

modalities.note: Preserve original text-only modalities. Oracle explicitly excludes images/files and the original launch says a multimodal variant was still in training. Current Build 0.1 aliases do not change this historical model.

reasoning.note: Original release/card and provider documentation explicitly identify reasoning, including streamed summarized traces.

tool_call.note: Original model performs iterative tool calls in coding harnesses, and providers explicitly support API function calling.

description.value: Text-only reasoning model for coding tasks and tool use in agentic programming environments.

sources.label: Cursor identifies sonic as Grok Code Fast 1

patch.notes: August 20, 2025 is the earliest documented public sonic preview, later identified as Grok Code Fast 1; the named Cursor/Copilot rollout was August 26 and xAI announcement August 28. Multiple preview checkpoints were used. Total and active parameters and neural architecture remain undisclosed in the primary sources checked; unsupported 314B/MoE directory claims are not adopted. Original text-only 256000-token specifications are preserved. The May 15, 2026 retirement guide redirects the original slug to Grok Build 0.1; current alias documentation describes that replacement, not the original weights.

summary: Corrected name, earliest documented public preview date and proprietary classification; replaced generic description. Independently preserved original 256K text-only reasoning/tool specifications despite current alias routing to multimodal Build 0.1. Original/later cards and targeted training/disclosure searches do not support numerical counts or topology; rejected unsupported third-party 314B/MoE claims.
